questions.question: The downstream farmers harmed by the tannery's effluent are bearing:
options: A negative externality — a cost outside the transaction

questions.question: When a polluter escapes part of its true production cost, the polluting product is:
The tragedy of the commons arises because each user of an unowned resource:
options: Captures the whole gain of extra use while depletion is shared by all
Pays the full cost of depletion personally
Is legally barred from using more

questions.question: Which South African case most directly illustrates commons pressure?
options: The carbon tax on large emitters
Overstocked communal rangelands carrying more animals than they can regrow

subtopics.title: Protecting the Environment — the Policy Toolbox

questions.question: Emission ceilings, compulsory environmental impact assessments and closed fishing seasons belong to:
The carbon tax corrects the externality because it:
options: Replaces the zero price on emissions with a real cost the polluter must face

questions.question: A tradable permit scheme meets the pollution cap at the lowest total cost because:
options: Firms that abate cheaply cut more and sell spare permits to firms that cannot
All firms must reduce emissions by the same amount
The state buys back every permit annually
Permits are issued without any cap

questions.question: Vesting fishing rights in a named coastal community protects the stock because:
options: The community is banned from fishing
An owner conserves when the resource's future value belongs to her

subtopics.title: Sustainability — Living Off the Interest, Not the Capital

questions.question: The Brundtland definition requires meeting present needs:
options: Without compromising future generations' ability to meet their own needs

questions.question: 'Living off the interest' of natural capital means:
options: Harvesting no faster than the stock replaces itself
Spending the stock slowly rather than quickly
Refusing to use natural resources at all

questions.question: A renewable resource behaves like a non-renewable when:
options: It is placed under state control
Harvesting exceeds the critical regeneration rate and the stock spirals down
It is exported rather than consumed locally

questions.question: For non-renewables such as platinum and coal, sustainable use means:
options: Extracting as fast as world prices allow
Waiting for the orebody to regenerate
Converting once-off proceeds into durable assets like skills and infrastructure

subtopics.title: The Global and Local Impact on South Africa

questions.question: The moral geometry of climate negotiations is that:
options: The North grew rich on two centuries of emissions while the South absorbs the earliest, heaviest damage
Africa emits the majority of world greenhouse gases
Emissions harm only the country that produces them
The South industrialised before the North

questions.question: The April 2022 KwaZulu-Natal floods are cited as evidence of:
options: The violent-rainfall end of a warming climate — over four hundred deaths and billions in damage
Falling sea levels on the east coast

questions.question: Carbon border charges threaten South African exports because:
options: They apply only to agricultural goods
They fix the rand's exchange rate
Goods made with coal-fired electricity pay a climate penalty at the customer's border
They prohibit all trade with Africa

questions.question: South Africa's triple climate exposure is as:
options: Heavy polluter, early victim and coal-dependent exporter

questions.question: In the smelter story, the 'unposted bill' lands on:
options: The township under the ash, which never signed the deal
The builders who buy steel rods

questions.question: Because the smelter never pays for the ash, the market:
options: Prices steel rods too low and keeps the furnace running longer
Charges builders extra for the damage

questions.question: Forty families each adding one more cow turn the shared field to dust because each family:
options: Gains the whole cow while the thinner grass is a shared loss

questions.question: Whose needs carry a price of exactly zero in both stories?
options: Future generations, who buy nothing in today's markets

subtopics.title: Putting a Price on the Smoke

questions.question: The plastic bag levy changes behaviour because:
options: A bag that costs something gets thought about instead of taken for free

questions.question: Once every ton of greenhouse gas has a price, cutting emissions becomes:
options: Cost-saving rather than charity — self-interest is hired to clean up

questions.question: A grazing committee that fences camps and rotates herds saves the field because:
options: Ownership makes one more cow eat your own next year, so users stop at the limit

questions.question: Countries sign climate treaties together mainly because:
options: One clean country in a dirty world pays much and fixes little — signing together stops free-riding

questions.question: 'Eat the harvest, never the seed' translates into economics as:
options: Draw on natural stocks more slowly than they renew

questions.question: The spaza owner eating the stock money warns that once-off mineral wealth should be:
options: Spent on consumption while it lasts
Turned into lasting assets — schooling, railways, industries with second acts

questions.question: 'Fence off a reserve while the village beside it goes hungry, and the fence will not survive the village' tests which pillar?
options: The social pillar — costs and benefits must be shared fairly

questions.question: South Africa's just transition aims to:
options: Keep every coal station open indefinitely
Abandon Mpumalanga's workers to the market
Close the coal era without closing the coal towns — clean power, retraining and regional rebuilding, part-financed by richer nations
